pĕremptālis , e, adj. peremptus,
I.of or belonging to destruction or abolition, abolishing, cancelling; only in augural lang., fulmina, lightnings that destroy the effect or portent of former lightnings: “peremptalia fulgura Gracchus ait vocari, quae superiora fulgura aut portenta vi suā perimant,” Fest. p. 214 Müll.: “peremptalia fulmina, quibus tolluntur priorum fulminum minae,” Sen. Q. N. 2, 49, 2 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
